title: Zee Learn: The Guarantee Comes Due

beats.say: On the twenty sixth of September, an asset reconstruction company served notice on Zee Learn. It has asked the insolvency tribunal to start insolvency proceedings against the company and its subsidiary, alleging a default of about eight hundred and twenty one crore rupees.
beats.cap: On 26 September, an asset reconstruction company served notice on Zee Learn. It has asked the insolvency tribunal to start insolvency proceedings against the company and its subsidiary, alleging a default of about ₹821 crore.
cues: On 26 September, an asset reconstruction company served notice on Zee Learn.
It has asked the insolvency tribunal to start insolvency proceedings against
the company and its subsidiary, alleging a default of about ₹821 crore.

beats.say: Ten days earlier, the same creditor had invoked Zee Learn's corporate guarantee and demanded eight hundred and eighteen crore rupees. For most of the previous year, Zee Learn's filings had reported the opposite: lenders withdrawing cases.
beats.cap: Ten days earlier, the same creditor had invoked Zee Learn's corporate guarantee and demanded ₹818.23 crore. For most of the previous year, Zee Learn's filings had reported the opposite: lenders withdrawing cases.
cues: Ten days earlier, the same creditor had invoked Zee Learn's corporate
guarantee and demanded ₹818.23 crore.
For most of the previous year, Zee Learn's filings had reported the opposite:
lenders withdrawing cases.

beats.say: This is the story of a guarantee that became larger than the company that gave it, told only from Zee Learn's own filings.
beats.cap: This is the story of a guarantee that became larger than the company that gave it, told only from Zee Learn's own filings.
cues: This is the story of a guarantee that became larger than the company that
gave it, told only from Zee Learn's own filings.

beats.say: Chapter one. A year of withdrawals.
beats.cap: Chapter one. A year of withdrawals.
cues: Chapter one.
A year of withdrawals.

beats.say: The debts are not Zee Learn's own operating loans. They come from guarantees that Zee Learn and its subsidiary Digital Ventures gave for loans taken by others: four trusts or entities that the filings never name.
beats.cap: The debts are not Zee Learn's own operating loans. They come from guarantees that Zee Learn and its subsidiary Digital Ventures gave for loans taken by others: "four trusts/entity" that the filings never name.
cues: The debts are not Zee Learn's own operating loans.
They come from guarantees that Zee Learn and its subsidiary Digital Ventures
gave for loans taken by others:
"four trusts/entity" that the filings never name.

beats.say: Yes Bank invoked those guarantees, with a claim of about four hundred and fifty crore rupees including interest to July twenty twenty one. In twenty twenty three, a settlement of two hundred and eighty five crore rupees was agreed with J C Flowers, which had bought the debt. It was terminated in October twenty twenty four, due to delays in payments.
beats.cap: Yes Bank invoked those guarantees, with a claim of ₹449.63 crore including interest to July 2021. In 2023, a ₹285 crore settlement was agreed with J.C. Flowers, which had bought the debt. It was terminated in October 2024, "due to delays in payments".
cues: Yes Bank invoked those guarantees, with a claim of ₹449.63 crore including
interest to July 2021.
In 2023, a ₹285 crore settlement was agreed with J.C.
Flowers, which had bought the debt.
It was terminated in October 2024, "due to delays in payments".

beats.say: The debt then passed to Assets Care and Reconstruction Enterprise, known as ACRE. In March twenty twenty five, Axis Bank's loans to the subsidiary were also assigned to ACRE. One creditor now held both sets of claims.
beats.cap: The debt then passed to Assets Care & Reconstruction Enterprise (ACRE). In March 2025, Axis Bank's loans to the subsidiary were also assigned to ACRE. One creditor now held both sets of claims.
cues: The debt then passed to Assets Care & Reconstruction Enterprise (ACRE).
In March 2025, Axis Bank's loans to the subsidiary were also assigned to ACRE.
One creditor now held both sets of claims.

beats.say: Then came a run of withdrawals. The subsidiary's insolvency process was withdrawn in December twenty twenty five, approved by ninety six percent of its creditors. Axis Bank's petition against Zee Learn was dismissed as withdrawn in March. And in June, the lenders told the tribunal they had decided to withdraw the remaining petition.
beats.cap: Then came a run of withdrawals. The subsidiary's insolvency process was withdrawn in December 2025, approved by 96.05% of its creditors. Axis Bank's petition against Zee Learn was dismissed as withdrawn in March 2026. And in June, the lenders told the tribunal they had decided to withdraw the remaining petition.
cues: Then came a run of withdrawals.
The subsidiary's insolvency process was withdrawn in December 2025,
approved by 96.05% of its creditors.
Axis Bank's petition against Zee Learn was dismissed as withdrawn in March
And in June, the lenders told the tribunal they had decided to withdraw the
remaining petition.

beats.say: The June filing recorded it plainly: the lender has decided to withdraw the Company Petition.
beats.cap: The June filing recorded it plainly: "the lender has decided to withdraw the Company Petition".
cues: The June filing recorded it plainly:
"the lender has decided to withdraw the Company Petition".

beats.say: Three months later, the direction reversed. On the sixteenth of September, ACRE invoked the guarantee and demanded eight hundred and eighteen point two three crore rupees. On the twenty sixth, it served notice of fresh insolvency petitions.
beats.cap: Three months later, the direction reversed. On 16 September, ACRE invoked the guarantee and demanded ₹818.23 crore. On 26 September, it served notice of fresh insolvency petitions.
cues: Three months later, the direction reversed.
On 16 September, ACRE invoked the guarantee and demanded ₹818.23 crore.
On 26 September, it served notice of fresh insolvency petitions.

beats.say: Chapter two. Why the guarantee matters.
beats.cap: Chapter two. Why the guarantee matters.
cues: Chapter two.
Why the guarantee matters.

beats.say: Zee Learn's own business is modest and profitable. In the last financial year, standalone revenue was three hundred and twelve point six crore rupees, and profit after tax ninety point six crore, including a one off write back of forty point six crore.
beats.cap: Zee Learn's own business is modest and profitable. In FY26, standalone revenue was ₹312.57 crore, and profit after tax ₹90.57 crore, including a one-off write-back of ₹40.58 crore.
cues: Zee Learn's own business is modest and profitable.
In FY26, standalone revenue was ₹312.57 crore,
and profit after tax ₹90.57 crore, including a one-off write-back of ₹40.58
crore.

beats.say: The guarantee is on a different scale. At the end of June, the accounts put the amount payable to ACRE at six hundred and sixty seven crore rupees. Against that, Zee Learn records almost eight hundred crore rupees as recoverable from the four trusts or entities.
beats.cap: The guarantee is on a different scale. At 30 June 2026, the accounts put the amount payable to ACRE at ₹667.46 crore. Against that, Zee Learn records ₹799.93 crore as recoverable from the four trusts/entity.
cues: The guarantee is on a different scale.
At 30 June 2026, the accounts put the amount payable to ACRE at ₹667.46 crore.
Against that, Zee Learn records ₹799.93 crore as recoverable from the four
trusts/entity.

beats.say: Zee Learn's standalone equity in March was two hundred and fifty four crore rupees. The amount it expects to recover from others is more than three times its equity.
beats.cap: Zee Learn's standalone equity at 31 March 2026 was ₹253.85 crore. The amount it expects to recover from others is more than three times its equity.
cues: Zee Learn's standalone equity at 31 March 2026 was ₹253.85 crore.
The amount it expects to recover from others is more than three times its
equity.

beats.say: Management's view is that the debt will be paid through monetising assets. And the company has been paying: fifty three crore rupees towards the guarantee last year, after thirty seven crore the year before.
beats.cap: Management's view is that the debt will be paid through monetising assets. And the company has been paying: ₹53 crore towards the guarantee in FY26, after ₹37 crore in FY25.
cues: Management's view is that the debt will be paid through monetising assets.
And the company has been paying:
₹53 crore towards the guarantee in FY26, after ₹37 crore in FY25.

beats.cap: Chapter three. What the auditor said.

beats.say: The auditor gave a qualified review of the June quarter. First, the eight hundred crore recoverable has not been assessed for impairment, so the auditor said it was unable to comment on the adjustments needed.
beats.cap: The auditor gave a qualified review of the June quarter. First, the ₹799.93 crore recoverable has not been assessed for impairment, so the auditor said it was "unable to comment upon adjustments".
cues: The auditor gave a qualified review of the June quarter.

beats.say: Second, despite two lenders invoking guarantees, the company has not provided for any liability against them.
beats.cap: Second, despite two lenders invoking guarantees, "the Company has not provided for any liability" against them.
cues: Second, despite two lenders invoking guarantees,
"the Company has not provided for any liability" against them.

beats.say: And separately, the auditor flagged a material uncertainty relating to going concern. All of this was written before September's demand and petitions.

beats.cap: Chapter four. The case both ways.

beats.say: The record so far favours settlement. Every earlier insolvency action in these filings was reversed, withdrawn, or the lender said it would withdraw. The new petitions have not yet been admitted, and the operating business grew last quarter.
beats.cap: The record so far favours settlement. Every earlier insolvency action in these filings was reversed, withdrawn, or the lender said it would withdraw. The new petitions have not yet been admitted, and the operating business grew last quarter.

beats.say: Now the bear case. One creditor now holds every claim. The June signal was reversed. The balance sheet depends on others paying. A settlement has failed before. And if a petition is admitted, a resolution professional takes charge and the board's powers are suspended.
